review_basis: Fact statement matched an existing Topic Pack anchor
Technical cross-check against authoritative standards, official documentation, or reproducible derivation is recorded per Fact
WordPress source references are retained as provenance but are not a prerequisite for factual verification
approval_record.approval_scope: independently verified facts across reviewed Topic Packs; all entries remain score-neutral

facts.statement: 균일한 액체에서 침수체적 V_sub의 부력은 F_b = rho g V_sub이다. 액위 변화가 침수체적과 겉보기 무게를 바꾼다.

verification_refs.citation: ABB, A dozen ways to measure fluid level and how they work
verification_refs.locator: Displacers and Figure 2
verification_refs.supports_claim: ABB explains that a suspended displacer experiences an upward force equal to the weight of liquid displaced; the immersed volume changes with level and the support force decreases. Multiplying displaced volume by density and gravitational acceleration gives F_b=rho*g*V_sub in SI force units.

facts.statement: 설계 액체 밀도와 실제 밀도가 달라지면 같은 잠김 체적의 부력이 달라져 레벨 지시가 편향될 수 있다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 2502 Controllers Instruction Manual D200126X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 4.1, Wet Calibration and Determining Suspended Weight; Section 7 troubleshooting
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual requires compensation when calibration-liquid specific gravity differs from process liquid, gives suspended-weight equations containing process specific gravity, and identifies deviation from design specific gravity as a reason for off-setpoint behavior.

facts.statement: 고정·현수된 displacer는 부력에 따른 힘 변화를 검출하고 자유 Float는 액면을 따라 움직이는 위치를 검출한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Level Controllers—Float-style and Displacer-style Level Sensing
verification_refs.locator: Level Controller Sensing Types
verification_refs.supports_claim: Emerson distinguishes a floating device that rises and falls with the liquid surface from a suspended displacer whose buoyancy changes the force on its spring or torque-tube suspension and is converted to a level signal.

facts.statement: Caged/외부 챔버와 cageless/용기 내 설치의 공정 연결·격리·접근성을 구별하고 침적·부착·마찰, 압력·온도 정격을 점검한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 2502 Controllers Instruction Manual D200126X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 2.1 and 2.5–2.6, caged/cageless mounting; Table 1 ratings; Section 7 maintenance
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual distinguishes external caged from vessel-mounted cageless constructions, specifies equalizing connections, shutoff valves and drains, warns that cage or stillwell contact creates erroneous output, discusses sediment clogging, and sets construction-specific pressure/temperature limits and maintenance precautions.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 249 Caged Sensors Instruction Manual D200099X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 2.1 Cleaning the Cage and Section 2.2 Removing the Displacer and Stem
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manufacturer states that process residue in a cage or connections can restrict flow or displacer movement, buildup on the displacer or stem changes weight or displacement, and cleaning requires pressure isolation and drainage.

facts.statement: 두 비혼합 액체의 계면 측정은 각 액체의 밀도와 침수체적 배분에 의존한다. 전체 침수·균일 밀도 조건이면 F_b = g(rho_L V_L + rho_U V_U)이고 V_L+V_U는 일정해 계면 감도가 밀도차에 비례한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 2502 Controllers Instruction Manual D200126X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 4.1, Determining Suspended Weight for Calibration, interface equation; Section 2.6 fully submerged condition
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual gives interface suspended weight as displacer weight minus the sum of lighter- and heavier-liquid specific-gravity-times-volume terms, and requires complete immersion for interface operation. Converting specific gravity to density yields the stated buoyancy sum; with constant total immersed volume its derivative with interface displacement is proportional to the density difference.

facts.statement: 지지된 displacer의 부력 변화는 토크튜브에 전달되어 비틀림·각도 변화를 만들고 전송기 또는 제어기 출력으로 변환된다. 출력 방향은 장치 구성에 따른다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 249 Caged Sensors Instruction Manual D200099X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 1.2 Description, torque-tube principle and rotary signal conversion
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual traces displaced-liquid buoyancy through displacer rod angular movement, torque-tube twist, rotary shaft and pneumatic/electric controller or transmitter output.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 2502 Controllers Instruction Manual D200126X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 2.4 Controller-Sensor Action
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual distinguishes direct and reverse action and notes mounting orientation affects output direction.

facts.statement: Wet calibration은 적절한 비중의 시험액으로 응답을 확인하고 다른 비중이면 침수량을 환산한다. Dry calibration은 제조사 절차의 등가 하중·추로 부력을 모사하며 실제 운전 유체 검증과 구별한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher 2502 Controllers Instruction Manual D200126X012, July 2024
verification_refs.locator: Section 4.1, Precalibration Requirements, Wet Calibration, Dry Calibration and Suspended Weight
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual differentiates in-service calibration from shop wet/dry procedures, requires specific-gravity compensation for substitute water, and simulates the process input in dry calibration using a calculated suspended weight.

facts.statement: IEC 60534-9은 응답시험의 valve·actuator·positioner 구성과 결과에 영향을 주는 조건을 기록하고, baseline·small-step·response-time 시험 및 측정 변수를 정한다. 개선 전후 비교에서는 해당 configuration과 시험조건을 비교 가능하게 유지해야 한다. 실제 PV variability·품질·에너지·air consumption은 공정별로 선정할 application KPI이며, 표준이 모든 현장에 공통으로 요구하는 목록은 아니다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-9:2007, Industrial-process control valves—Part 9: Test procedure for response measurements from step inputs
verification_refs.supports_claim: The standard defines baseline, small-step and response-time tests; requires the relevant valve configuration and results-affecting characteristics to be recorded; distinguishes bench, laboratory and in-process tests and measured variables. It does not prescribe a universal before-after operational KPI list.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-9:2007 standard text preview
verification_refs.supports_claim: Provides the corresponding normative test setup, reporting, process-variable measurement, and test-procedure clauses.

facts.statement: 제어밸브는 유체 유량을 조작해 공정변수를 설정값에 가깝게 유지하는 최종제어요소다. 제어밸브의 deadband·stiction 같은 비선형성은 제어루프 성능을 제한할 수 있으므로, 밸브 응답 특성이 공정변수 제어 성능에 영향을 줄 수 있다. 영향의 크기와 실제 공정변동은 해당 밸브와 루프 조건으로 확인해야 한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, 6th edition, Chapter 1 overview
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 1 overview, What is a Control Valve?
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that the control valve manipulates fluid flow to compensate for load disturbance and keep the regulated process variable close to setpoint.

verification_refs.citation: S. Choudhury, N. F. Thornhill, and S. L. Shah, ‘Modelling valve stiction,’ Control Engineering Practice 13(5), 2005, pp. 641–658, doi:10.1016/j.conengprac.2004.05.005
verification_refs.locator: Abstract
verification_refs.supports_claim: The abstract states that control-valve nonlinearities such as stiction and deadband limit control-loop performance; it does not quantify a universal process-variable variability increase.

facts.statement: Fisher 3660 positioner는 feedback lever와 range spring으로 stem 움직임을 positioner에 되돌려 pressure 출력을 조절한다. 별도로 Fisher 1052 actuator는 clamped shaft lever와 single-pivot linkage로 actuator–valve lost motion을 줄인다. 따라서 positioner feedback/tuning과 기계적 linkage lost motion은 서로 다른 문제이며, 해당 자료는 positioner 조정이 유격을 물리적으로 제거한다고 말하지 않는다. 이 설명은 문서화된 Fisher 구성에 한정된다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, 3660 and 3661 Positioners Instruction Manual, D101402X012
verification_refs.locator: p. 28, Principle of Operation; Figure 23
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes stem movement fed back to the beam through a feedback lever and range spring, which changes flapper position and prevents further relay output pressure increase at the new position.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, 1051 and 1052 Style F and G Size 40, 60, and 70 Rotary Actuators Instruction Manual Supplement, D103790X012
verification_refs.locator: p. 3, Product Description
verification_refs.supports_claim: States the 1052 actuator linkage uses a clamped shaft lever and single pivot point to reduce lost motion between the actuator and valve.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Fisher 1052 Rotary Actuators product page
verification_refs.locator: Product description and key features
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes the 1052 single-joint linkage with splined/clamped lever as minimizing lost motion and improving control accuracy.

facts.statement: IEC 60534-4의 dead-band test는 약 25%, 50%, 75% rated travel 위치에서 입력 방향을 반전시켜 stem/shaft 움직임을 반전시키는 데 필요한 operating-signal 변화를 측정한다. 표준은 dead band와 hysteresis를 별도 정의하므로 두 값을 같은 용어로 취급하지 않는다. 이는 정해진 시험 구성의 시험이며 모든 process-loaded 성능을 직접 보증하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-4:2021, Industrial-process control valves—Part 4: Inspection and routine testing
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines dead band and hysteresis separately; §4.6 states that the dead-band test measures operating-signal change required to reverse stem/shaft motion at about 25%, 50%, and 75% rated travel. §5.8 specifies the test boundary and procedure.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-4:2021 standard text preview
verification_refs.supports_claim: Reproduces the standard's definitions and dead-band test purpose, measurement positions, assembly boundary, and test method.

facts.statement: IEC 60534-9은 valve resolution을 같은 방향 입력에서 출력 움직임이 관찰되는 최소 입력 step으로 정의하고, instrument resolution은 valve resolution의 1/3 이하(권장 1/10 이하)로 구별해 제시한다. 따라서 측정기 신호 분해능과 밸브 자체의 step-movement 특성을 같은 값으로 취급하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-9:2007, Industrial-process control valves—Part 9: Test procedure for response measurements from step inputs
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines valve resolution as the smallest input increment in one direction for which output movement is observed; separately requires instrument resolution no greater than one third of valve resolution, preferably one tenth; §8.2 specifies the small-step test for dead band and resolution.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-9:2007 standard text preview
verification_refs.supports_claim: Provides the valve-resolution definition, separate instrument-resolution criteria, and small-step test purpose.

facts.statement: Emerson/Fisher Control Valve Handbook Figure 2.4는 Valve A의 같은 크기 step에서 opening과 closing 응답시간을 각각 측정하며, 2% step의 예에서는 Td가 각각 0.25 s와 0.50 s, T63이 0.34 s와 0.74 s로 다르다. 따라서 이 사례에서는 응답방향을 구분해 보고해야 한다. 수치는 해당 valve assembly와 시험조건의 예이며 보편적 비대칭 크기나 원인을 뜻하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, 6th edition
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 2, Figure 2.4, Valve Response Time Summary, Valve A, 2% step rows
verification_refs.supports_claim: The table gives Valve A opening 2% step Td/T63 = 0.25/0.34 seconds and closing 2% step (−2%) Td/T63 = 0.50/0.74 seconds. These are product-assembly test data, not universal values or causal findings.

facts.statement: Positioner는 actuator에 전달되는 pressure를 조절하지만 actuator 자체의 가용 thrust를 대체하지 않는다. Fisher 685SR sizing 사례는 서비스 하중·unbalance·seat load·packing friction으로 필요한 valve thrust를 산정하고, 공급압력·actuator 크기·spring 조건에서의 가용 thrust와 비교한다. 가용 thrust가 부족하면 더 큰 actuator를 선정해 sizing을 반복해야 한다. 수치는 해당 밸브·액추에이터·서비스 조건에 한정된다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Catalog 14, Fisher 685SR Spring Retract Piston Actuator sizing example
verification_refs.locator: 685SR Pressure-Tends-to-Open sizing calculation, Catalog pp. B-80.3–B-80.4
verification_refs.supports_claim: The example computes required valve thrust including unbalance, seat load and packing friction, compares it with actuator thrust at the available supply pressure and spring conditions, finds size 10 insufficient, and repeats the calculation with a larger size 12 actuator.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, FIELDVUE DVC6200 SIS Digital Valve Controller Instruction Manual, D103557X012
verification_refs.locator: Table 1, p. 5, pneumatic output specification
verification_refs.supports_claim: Specifies the positioner's pneumatic output as up to full supply pressure; it does not replace the actuator-level required-versus-available thrust calculation.

facts.statement: Emerson/Fisher Control Valve Handbook은 hunting을 외부 자극이 사라진 뒤에도 지속되는 유의한 진동으로 정의하고, 안정한계 부근의 운전을 나타낼 수 있다고 설명한다. 제어밸브에서는 control system 또는 valve positioner의 불안정으로 actuator loading pressure가 진동하는 형태로 나타날 수 있다. 이는 가능한 원인 중 하나를 제시하며 모든 현장 진동의 원인을 확정하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, 6th edition
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 1, hunting terminology; Chapter 2, §2.1.3.3, positioner/actuator loop stability
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook defines hunting as appreciable oscillation continuing after external stimuli disappear and says it can indicate operation at/near the stability limit. For control valves it describes actuator loading-pressure oscillation caused by control-system or valve-positioner instability; Chapter 2 explains that excessive positioner/actuator loop gain can destabilize an assembly.

facts.statement: Fisher FIELDVUE DVC6200 SIS의 공압 연결·용량 요구는 relay 구성별로 다르다. 제조사는 Low Bleed Relay에 3/8 in tubing을 권장하고, High Cv relay에는 port connection size 이상 tubing을 권장하며, relay별 출력용량과 허용 공급압력도 별도로 규정한다. 이 제품별 사양만으로 모든 positioner의 배관 길이·내경과 응답시간 관계를 일반화하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, FIELDVUE DVC6200 SIS Digital Valve Controller Instruction Manual, D103557X012
verification_refs.locator: Table 1, pp. 5–6: supply pressure, output capacity, connections and recommended tubing size
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual specifies model/relay-dependent supply-pressure and output-capacity data; recommends 3/8 in tubing for the Low Bleed Relay; recommends tubing at least equal to the port connection size for High Cv; and provides no universal quantitative law relating tubing length or inside diameter to response time.

facts.statement: Fisher VBL은 positioner와 함께 throttling valve actuator의 stroking speed를 높이며, 큰 입력 변화에는 booster가 공급·배기 포트를 열어 고유량을 전달한다. 안정성을 위해 integral bypass를 조정해 큰 변화에는 booster가 동작하고 작은 positioner 신호는 bypass를 통해 전달되도록 한다. 제조사는 부적절한 구성의 positioner saturation 가능성도 명시한다. 이는 Fisher VBL의 제품별 동작·조정 지침이다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, VBL Volume Booster Instruction Manual, D103317X012
verification_refs.locator: §1.2 Description, p. 2; §3 Operating Information, p. 7; §4 Principle of Operation, p. 8
verification_refs.supports_claim: States the VBL is used with a positioner to increase stroking speed; the bypass must be adjusted for stable operation; large rapid signals open supply/exhaust for high-volume flow while small signal changes pass through bypass; the described features address positioner saturation risk.

facts.statement: Fisher FIELDVUE DVC6200 SIS의 travel tuning set은 C에서 가장 느린 응답, M에서 가장 빠른 응답을 제공한다. 제조사는 밸브 조립체가 불안정하면 response를 낮추고 sluggish하면 response를 높이도록 안내하며, 사전 설정값은 초기값이므로 실제 valve·actuator 응답을 확인해 조정해야 한다. 이는 해당 제품의 튜닝 지침이며 모든 positioner의 gain–air-consumption 관계를 일반화하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, FIELDVUE DVC6200 SIS Digital Valve Controller Instruction Manual, D103557X012
verification_refs.locator: pp. 24–26, Travel Tuning and initial actuator/tuning set guidance; p. 29, Stabilize/Optimize
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual identifies set C as the slowest and M as the fastest response, says tuning sets are recommended starting points that may need adjustment for the actual assembly, and directs decrease response for instability and increase response for sluggish operation. It is product-specific and does not support universal air-consumption claims.

facts.statement: 100% full-stroke step test는 지정된 방향의 입력 변화에 대해 valve assembly가 전체 travel을 완료하는 시간을 측정한다. 결과는 시험한 stroke direction과 step 조건으로 보고하고, 공압 공급·배기 제한이나 saturation의 원인은 travel과 actuator pressure/supply condition을 함께 조사해 진단한다. Full-stroke time만으로 그 원인이나 작은 신호 성능을 확정할 수 없다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, 6th edition, Chapter 2: Control Valve Performance
verification_refs.locator: §2.1.3.6 Valve Response Time and Figure 2.4 full-stroke/step-response table
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes a stroking-time test as a 100% input step and measurement of time for the assembly to complete full stroke in either direction; distinguishes this test from typical small process-control changes and reports directional response values.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-9:2007, Industrial-process control valves—Part 9: Test procedure for response measurements from step inputs
verification_refs.locator: Official publication scope
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines testing and reporting of step response for the complete valve assembly; it does not equate measured total stroke time with a unique pneumatic failure diagnosis.

facts.statement: Small-step response 시험은 실제 제어에 가까운 작은 input step에 대한 valve stem/shaft 응답을 측정해 작은 신호에서의 deadband, resolution 및 response 특성을 평가한다. 100% full-stroke time 시험은 전체 stroke 속도를 평가하며, 일반적인 작은 제어변화에 대한 성능을 대신하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60534-9:2007, Industrial-process control valves—Part 9: Test procedure for response measurements from step inputs
verification_refs.locator: Official publication scope
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines testing, measuring, and reporting control-valve assembly step response in an open-loop environment to characterize response to input signal changes; the tested assembly includes valve body, actuator, and required accessories such as positioner.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, 6th edition, Chapter 2: Control Valve Performance
verification_refs.locator: §2.1.2 deadband/resolution and §2.1.3 response time; full-stroke vs small-signal discussion
verification_refs.supports_claim: Distinguishes deadband/resolution and small-signal response from a 100% input-step stroking-time test, noting that full stroking time does not indicate typical small control-movement performance.

facts.statement: Valve response time은 command 변화 후 움직임 시작 전 dead time과 움직임 시작 후 목표 변화에 접근하는 dynamic time으로 구분할 수 있다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, 6th edition, Chapter 2: Control Valve Performance
verification_refs.locator: §2.1.3.1 Dead Time and §2.1.3.2 Dynamic Time
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines the initial dead-time interval before valve motion and the dynamic-time portion after motion begins; explains that dynamic time is primarily determined by positioner/actuator characteristics and reports step responses with dead time and T63 metrics.

facts.statement: Stiction이 있는 밸브는 제어 입력이 변해도 정지해 있다가 마찰 한계를 넘으면 위치가 jump할 수 있고, 특정 공정·제어기 동특성 조합에서는 폐루프 process-variable oscillation 또는 limit cycle을 유발할 수 있다. Deadband만으로 limit cycle이 항상 생긴다고 일반화할 수 없으며, PI loop에서 plant integrator가 없는 경우 순수 deadband/backlash는 limit cycle을 만들지 않는 조건도 보고되어 있다.

verification_refs.citation: M. A. A. S. Choudhury, S. L. Shah, and N. F. Thornhill, “Modelling valve stiction,” Control Engineering Practice, vol. 13, pp. 641–658, 2005
verification_refs.locator: §4, pp. 648–649 (deadband/friction and jumping behavior); §6, pp. 653–654 (conditional limit-cycle analysis)
verification_refs.supports_claim: The paper distinguishes deadband from stiction, describes valve jumping when static friction is overcome, reports stiction-induced closed-loop oscillation/limit-cycle behavior under modeled conditions, and states that pure deadband/backlash cannot produce limit cycles with a PI controller unless the plant has an integrator. This supports a conditional mechanism, not a universal outcome.

facts.statement: Positioner는 command와 실제 stem 또는 shaft position의 차이를 이용해 actuator pressure를 조절하는 위치 피드백 장치이다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Valve Positioners product guide
verification_refs.locator: What Is a Valve Positioner? and How a Valve Positioner Works
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that positioners require stem/shaft position feedback and deliver pneumatic pressure to the actuator so valve position corresponds to the control-system setpoint.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, 3710 and 3720 Positioners Instruction Manual, D101728X012
verification_refs.locator: Principle of Operation, pp. 30–31
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes input force opposed by a feedback spring whose position is determined by the actuator feedback shaft/cam; spool outputs supply or vent actuator pressure until force balance is restored at the requested position.

facts.statement: IEC 60534-8-3 기반 제어밸브 aerodynamic-noise 예측은 밸브의 측정 가능한 geometry와 적용 service condition을 입력으로 한다. 따라서 서로 다른 운전조건의 결과를 하나의 예측값으로 대체하지 말고 각 지정 case의 입력으로 평가한다. Minimum·normal·maximum과 startup·shutdown을 모두 포함할지는 프로젝트에서 정의한 credible operating cases에 따른다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Sourcebook—Oil and Gas
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 6, Aerodynamic Noise Prediction; IEC 60534-8-3 method description
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes the IEC aerodynamic-noise prediction method as based on measurable valve geometry and service conditions applied to the valve. This supports case-dependent inputs but not a mandatory identical minimum/normal/maximum/startup/shutdown matrix for every project.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, noise considerations chapter
verification_refs.locator: Noise prediction method and service-condition discussion
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies flow conditions and valve geometry as inputs to the frequency-spectrum/noise calculation; it does not prescribe a universal operating-case inventory.

facts.statement: IECEx OD 504의 hazardous-area electrical-system design competence 기준은 분류된 장소에 맞는 장비·배선 선정 및 인증 적합성 확인을 포함한다. 설계 선택지를 정당화할 때 hazard risk, 기능 및 경제성도 고려한다. 이는 역량평가 범위이며 특정 보호방식의 보편적 우선순위나 단독 선택 알고리즘을 정하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: IECEx OD 504, Edition 4.0 (2021), Specification for Units of Competence assessment outcomes
verification_refs.supports_claim: OD 504 lists interpreting classification documents, selecting equipment and wiring for a given classified area, checking certification suitability, considering environmental conditions/maintenance and wiring load/duty, and justifying design options with hazard risk, functionality and economic considerations. It defines competency evidence, not a universal protection-method algorithm or priority.

facts.statement: 액체 밸브 sizing 결과를 교차 검산할 때는 동일한 유량·압력 단위와 실제 밸브 차압, 액체 비중 및 적용 sizing equation을 사용한다. 기본식의 전제(난류·비기화 등)가 맞지 않거나 배관/점도 보정이 적용되면 해당 계수와 보정식을 포함하며, vendor 계산과의 차이는 입력·계산 basis를 확인하는 신호이지 단독으로 오류를 확정하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Baker Hughes, Masoneilan Control Valve Sizing Handbook
verification_refs.locator: Liquid Flow Equations, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 4); actual valve pressure drop, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 3); nomenclature and correction-factor sections
verification_refs.supports_claim: Provides liquid sizing equations and their turbulent/non-vaporizing scope, identifies flow, specific gravity, pressure drop and applicable correction factors, and distinguishes actual valve pressure drop from total available system differential. This supports a reproducible same-basis check, not a universal mandatory hand-check or a guarantee of valve-selection correctness.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 5: Control Valve Sizing
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 5, liquid-flow equations and worked sizing examples
verification_refs.supports_claim: Documents the service inputs, unit-dependent equation constants, sizing coefficients and worked calculation sequence for liquid-service sizing; it supports independent reproduction only when the same inputs and applicable equation basis are used.

facts.statement: For Fisher 2625, 2625SST, and 2625NS volume boosters, the manufacturer describes a 1:1 device: within the designed deadband, output pressure is identical to input pilot pressure. This is model-specific; pressure ratios for other booster designs must be checked against their own documentation.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher 2625, 2625SST, and 2625NS Volume Boosters Instruction Manual Supplement, D103541X012
verification_refs.locator: Product/System Properties, item 4
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies the listed volume booster models as 1:1 devices with a designed deadband and states that input pressure produces identical output pressure within the deadband. The verification is explicitly limited to these models.

facts.statement: At constant temperature, the ideal-gas relation gives a tank gas-inventory change Δn = VΔP/(RT) over an absolute-pressure band. At the same mass-flow supply and demand conditions, a larger volume stores more gas and takes longer to charge; actual actuator pressure-support duration and response depend on leakage, load, pressure band, and supply/exhaust capacity.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible ideal-gas and mass-balance derivation
verification_refs.edition_or_version: Assumptions recorded in the Fact conditions; checked 2026-10-11
verification_refs.locator: Δn = VΔP/(RT); t = Δn/ṁ for constant mass flow ṁ
verification_refs.supports_claim: From pV=nRT at constant T, the gas inventory change across a pressure interval is Δn=VΔP/(RT), using absolute pressure. At fixed mass flow, the charge time for that inventory is t=Δn/ṁ, so it scales with V. This does not predict a universal hold time: leakage, actuator demand, regulator/booster capacity and operating pressure band are separate inputs.

facts.statement: Actuator fill/vent response depends on required gas inventory and the flow capacity of the positioner, booster, tubing, fittings, and actuator ports. Restrictive flow paths can create pressure loss and delay; Emerson's Fisher VBL manual directs sizing the piping and actuator input connections to meet capacity demand. Actual pressure drop and stroke time must be determined for the model and installation, not assumed from a universal tube size.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher VBL Volume Booster Instruction Manual, D103317X012
verification_refs.locator: §1.2 p. 2; Table 1 and Table 2 pp. 3–4; §2.2 p. 6; §3 p. 8
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes increased actuator stroking speed and high-volume output; gives model port/flow coefficients; instructs that piping be properly sized to meet booster capacity demand and actuator input connections be properly sized; calls for regulator capacity to meet stroking capacity requirements. Scope is the Fisher VBL installation guidance.

verification_refs.citation: Gas inventory balance and finite-flow-path pressure loss principle
verification_refs.edition_or_version: Engineering relation; conditions recorded in Fact; checked 2026-10-11
verification_refs.locator: At fixed state, required gas mass follows pV=nRT; filling time is required mass divided by delivered mass flow. A restrictive path has flow-dependent pressure loss.
verification_refs.supports_claim: The gas mass needed to move an actuator chamber through a defined pressure/volume state change and the mass flow available through ports and tubing determine fill/vent time. Finite flow resistance causes a pressure gradient under flow. Exact values require gas-state, path geometry, fitting, valve/booster capacity and actuator-load data; this derivation supports only the directional dependence, not a universal sizing value.

facts.statement: For positioner calibration or diagnostic work, distinguish and retain the as-found condition before adjustment from the as-left condition after adjustment/verification. Emerson describes capturing DVC6200 as-found data with a valve-signature diagnostic before calibration; NIST recommends pre- and post-calibration accuracy/precision data in calibration reports. The detailed fields and acceptance limits depend on the device and governing procedure; no universal fixed record set is asserted.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher FIELDVUE DVC6200 Digital Valve Controller Instruction Manual, D103409X012
verification_refs.locator: Calibration section, p. 80
verification_refs.supports_claim: Before initiating calibration to address suspected drift, the manual recommends a Valve Signature diagnostic test to capture as-found data for future root-cause analysis. This is a model-specific example, not a universal required procedure.

verification_refs.citation: NIST, Recommended Calibration Interval
verification_refs.locator: Q&A on recalibration reports
verification_refs.supports_claim: NIST says it does not set universal calibration intervals and advises that recalibration reports include as-submitted and post-calibration accuracy/precision data to validate or refine intervals. This supports keeping before/after results, not a universal positioner field list.

facts.statement: For an IEC 62382 control-stroke loop check, Annex A.4 gives full-stroke endpoints and intermediate 25%, 50%, and 75% travel as examples; intermediate points are checked in increasing and decreasing directions to detect hysteresis. The actual points and acceptance criteria are set for each project loop.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 62382:2024, Control systems in the process industry — Electrical and instrumentation loop check; ANSI/ISA-62382-2026 (IEC 62382:2024 IDT)
verification_refs.locator: Annex A.4, Actuators and valves, Control Stroke; §§6.1 and 6.2.4
verification_refs.supports_claim: The informative control-stroke example checks full stroke and intermediate positions such as 25%, 50%, and 75% in increasing and decreasing directions to detect hysteresis. The standard says actual tests and acceptance criteria are established for each loop/project; this is not a universal fixed calibration interval or all-points mandate.

facts.statement: IEC 62382 defines a functional loop check as exercising all loop components in one test to verify both individual and combined operation. The exact test method, order, device points, and acceptance criteria are planned for the specific loop; an electropneumatic valve may require checking applicable command, current, pressure, travel, and feedback points.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 62382:2024, Control systems in the process industry — Electrical and instrumentation loop check; ANSI/ISA-62382-2026 (IEC 62382:2024 IDT)
verification_refs.locator: §6.2.4; Annex A.1; Annex A.4
verification_refs.supports_claim: Clause 6.2.4 states that the functional check exercises all loop components during one test and verifies their individual and combined proper operation. The method/order is defined by the project team; Annex A notes that checks vary by component, signal type, tools, and project acceptance criteria.

facts.statement: IEC 62382 Annex A.4 gives simulation of an actuator failure, such as loss of air supply or electrical signal, as an example loop check to verify the correct reaction. Test scenarios and expected fail position depend on the installed loop design and planned acceptance criteria.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 62382:2024, Control systems in the process industry — Electrical and instrumentation loop check; ANSI/ISA-62382-2026 (IEC 62382:2024 IDT)
verification_refs.locator: Annex A.4, Actuators and valves
verification_refs.supports_claim: For control-stroke testing, Annex A.4 lists simulating actuator failure (e.g. loss of air supply and electric signal) to verify the correct reaction. It is an example within loop-check planning, not a universal fixed set of failure scenarios or a substitute for SIS validation.

facts.statement: IEC 62382 loop checking verifies the configured electrical/instrumentation loop's individual and combined functions against project criteria, but explicitly excludes validation of safety instrumented systems. An end-to-end valve loop check therefore cannot by itself claim SIS validation.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 62382:2024, Control systems in the process industry — Electrical and instrumentation loop check; ANSI/ISA-62382-2026 (IEC 62382:2024 IDT)
verification_refs.locator: §5.2 Excluded activities
verification_refs.supports_claim: Section 5.2 explicitly lists validation of safety instrumented systems as outside IEC 62382 loop-check activities.

facts.statement: Rosemount 5408에서 Upper Null Zone은 송신기 가까이의 에코를 무시하도록 설정되는 영역이며, 그 안에서는 level 측정이 수행되지 않는다. 따라서 이 모델의 Upper Range Value와 요구 측정범위는 manual에 따라 UNZ와 대조해 설정해야 한다. Petroleum storage tank overfill protection은 적용범위와 API Std 2350 category를 따른다. API 2350 범위의 Category 3은 ATG와 독립 LAHH sensor를 함께 사용하지만, 이를 모든 탱크·서비스의 보편 요구사항으로 확대하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Rosemount 5408 and 5408:SIS Level Transmitters Reference Manual
verification_refs.locator: §7.5.3 Upper Null Zone, p. 138
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines the Upper Null Zone as a near-transmitter region where echoes are ignored, states that measurements are not performed in it, and instructs that Upper Range Value be configured below the zone boundary.

verification_refs.citation: API Standard 2350, Overfill Prevention for Storage Tanks in Petroleum Facilities
verification_refs.edition_or_version: 5th edition (September 2020), Errata 1 April 2021; edition status checked 2026-10-11
verification_refs.locator: §5.2.4.1, Category 3 Facility
verification_refs.supports_claim: The Category 3 overfill prevention system uses both an automatic tank gauge and an independent LAHH sensor; API's catalog identifies the fifth edition and limits the standard to its petroleum-storage-tank scope.

verification_refs.citation: UK HSE, HSG176: The Storage of Flammable Liquids in Tanks
verification_refs.locator: Figure 9, p. 33
verification_refs.supports_claim: Illustrates LAHH as an independent alarm driven by a separate level sensor in the guidance's flammable-liquid storage-tank context.

facts.statement: Magnetrol Eclipse 706 manual은 single-rod GWR의 주변 전자기장이 설치·적용조건에 민감하며, 노즐의 임피던스 불연속과 가까운 금속 장애물이 추가 반사·허위에코 또는 오측정을 일으킬 수 있다고 설명한다. 같은 제품 구성에서 접지된 coaxial outer tube는 근접물체·노즐 영향이 줄어든다고 구분한다. 이 설명은 해당 제품의 probe 구성에 한정하며 모든 GWR probe의 전파모드를 일반화하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: AMETEK/Magnetrol, Eclipse Model 706 HART Installation and Operating Manual, BE 57-606
verification_refs.supports_claim: States single-rod performance depends on installation/application because its surrounding electromagnetic field is affected by nearby objects; nozzle-end impedance mismatch and metallic obstructions can produce reflections/false echoes or erroneous readings; the grounded coaxial outer tube in the described configuration reduces proximity/nozzle effects.

facts.statement: 레이저 삼각측량은 대상 거리와 검출기상의 spot 위치를 해당 센서의 기준선, 초점거리, 삼각측량각 및 검출기 위치 등 광학기하로 연결한다. 실제 광학계의 parameter tolerance와 aberration 때문에 거리변환은 설계값을 적용하거나 기준거리 측정값으로 보정할 수 있으며, mapping과 계수는 장치 구성에 종속된다.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Technical Note 1682, 3D Imaging Systems for Manufacturing, Construction, and Mobility
verification_refs.locator: §2.1, Fig. 8–9 and triangulation equations, p. 16
verification_refs.supports_claim: Presents active triangulation distance equations relating baseline distance, detector focal length, measured detector coordinate and scan angle, and analyzes uncertainty dependence on geometry and detector position.

verification_refs.citation: P. Kienle et al., Optical Setup for Error Compensation in a Laser Triangulation System, Sensors 20(17), 4949
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies baseline, focal length, detector offset and triangulation angle as optical setup parameters; says real production tolerances and optical aberrations make parameters imperfectly known and describes either calculating with known parameters or calibrating spot-position-to-distance mapping from measured data points.

facts.statement: 확산반사형 광전센서의 수광량 기반 검출에서는 대상 표면의 색과 매끄러움에 따라 반사광량, 동작 안정성과 sensing distance가 달라질 수 있으므로, 수광량만으로 장치 독립적인 절대거리를 정할 수 없다. 별도의 distance-setting 센서는 반사 spot 위치 또는 분할 수광소자 간 광량 차를 이용할 수 있어 두 방식을 구분한다.

verification_refs.citation: OMRON Industrial Automation, Overview of Photoelectric Sensors
verification_refs.locator: Classification, Diffuse-reflective Sensors, lines 161–173; distance-settable sensors, lines 194–206
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines diffuse-reflective sensing from received reflected-light intensity and states that reflected intensity, operating stability and sensing distance vary with target surface color and smoothness; separately describes distance-settable sensors using reflected-beam position on a detector.

verification_refs.citation: OMRON Industrial Automation, FAQ00320: By what principle is the distance-setting Photoelectric Sensor detected?
verification_refs.locator: Answer, lines 33–52
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that PSD distance-setting detects reflected spot position and that dual photodiode models compare the near/far receiving-light amounts to decide nearer/farther than a setting distance.

facts.statement: LVDT 특성화는 명시된 정격 여자 전압·주파수와 지정 stroke에서 기준 위치별 출력으로 선형성, 변환비, 위상, 영점 잔류전압 등을 평가할 수 있다. 측정결과의 계측학적 추적성은 측정시스템을 명시한 문서화된 교정사슬과 각 단계의 불확도로 뒷받침된다.

verification_refs.citation: North Atlantic Industries, Bench-Testing LVDT/RVDT Performance
verification_refs.locator: §§ What you measure; Test setup; Linearity and transformation ratio; Phase shift; Null voltage, lines 31–64
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes characterization at rated excitation voltage/frequency; known core positions; output linearity, transformation ratio, phase shift, and null voltage, using a position fixture and phase-angle voltmeter.

verification_refs.citation: NIST, Metrological Traceability: Frequently Asked Questions and NIST Policy
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines traceability as a property of a measurement result through a documented unbroken calibration chain contributing to uncertainty; requires describing the measurement system and associated uncertainty and clarifies that instruments themselves are not traceable.

facts.statement: LVDT 1차 권선의 여자를 과도하게 높이면 코어가 포화되어 2차 출력의 고조파가 증가할 수 있고, 자기재료의 포화는 규정 선형범위에서도 비선형을 일으킬 수 있다. 허용 여자 수준과 영향은 센서 모델별 정격·사양으로 확인한다.

verification_refs.citation: North Atlantic Industries, Bench-Testing LVDT/RVDT Performance
verification_refs.locator: § Maximum excitation (core saturation), lines 104–106
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that driving the primary too hard saturates the core and adds harmonics to the output; recommends determining the low-distortion excitation limit by monitoring secondary-output THD.

verification_refs.citation: Steve Arar, Introduction to Linear Variable Differential Transformers (LVDTs), All About Circuits
verification_refs.locator: § Linearity Error, lines 79–83
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies magnetic-material saturation as a mechanism of nonlinearity within the nominal linear range and notes that it can produce a third-harmonic component at null.

facts.statement: An overall sound level and a frequency-band spectrum (such as octave-band levels) report different information: the former is a total level for the stated measurement convention, while each band level reports sound power or pressure within a defined frequency band. A-weighting is an additional frequency weighting and is not interchangeable with an unweighted octave spectrum.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 13348:2019, Fans — Tolerances, methods of conversion and technical data presentation
verification_refs.locator: §§3.26–3.30, total and octave-band sound power/pressure levels
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines total sound power, octave-band sound power, A-weighted total sound power, total sound pressure and A-weighted sound pressure as distinct acoustic reporting quantities.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 3747:2010, Acoustics — Determination of sound power levels and sound energy levels of noise sources using sound pressure
verification_refs.locator: §3.2 notes on frequency-weighted and frequency-band-limited sound pressure
verification_refs.supports_claim: Separately identifies frequency-weighted or frequency-band-limited sound-pressure levels and requires the weighting/band to be indicated.

facts.statement: If parallel-valve and bypass acoustic sources are mutually uncorrelated and reported with the same reference and weighting, their combined sound level is found by summing their linear power (or mean-square-pressure) ratios and converting the result back to decibels; the dB values themselves are not directly added.

verification_refs.citation: Algebraic derivation from logarithmic sound-level definition and zero cross-correlation
verification_refs.locator: For mutually uncorrelated sources, add linear power ratios 10^(Li/10), then apply 10 log10 to the sum
verification_refs.supports_claim: The standard's level definitions and the linear power-addition relation give the logarithmic sum. The source independence and common measurement basis are explicit preconditions.

facts.statement: A-weighted sound pressure level (dBA or LpA) is a frequency-weighted measurement using the A-weighting response, which approximates human-ear frequency response for low-level sounds; it is not the same quantity as unweighted sound pressure level. The weighting label and measurement context should be retained, and dBA alone does not establish a site-specific occupational exposure limit.

verification_refs.citation: U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration, OSHA Technical Manual, Section III, Chapter 5: Noise
verification_refs.locator: Definitions, A-weighting; noise measurement discussion
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines A-weighting as approximating loudness relative to a 40-dB 1-kHz tone and says it best fits the frequency response of the human ear; explains that A-weighted instrument response differs from other weighting curves.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 3747:2010, Acoustics — Determination of sound power levels and sound energy levels of noise sources using sound pressure
verification_refs.locator: §3.2 Note 1
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that applied frequency weighting is indicated with subscripts and gives LpA as an example of A-weighted sound pressure level.

facts.statement: Sound power level is 10 log10(W/W0) dB, where W is the source sound power and W0 is the specified reference sound power (1 pW for airborne acoustics). It characterizes source power, not sound pressure at a particular receiver point.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 3747:2010, Acoustics — Determination of sound power levels and sound energy levels of noise sources using sound pressure
verification_refs.locator: §3.17 Sound power level
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines sound power level as ten times the base-10 logarithm of source sound power over reference sound power and gives the reference value as 1 pW.

facts.statement: Sound pressure level is 20 log10(prms/p0) dB (equivalently 10 log10(prms²/p0²)); for sound in air, the standard reference pressure is 20 μPa. It describes pressure at a measurement location and depends on the acoustic field and measurement conditions.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 3747:2010, Acoustics — Determination of sound power levels and sound energy levels of noise sources using sound pressure
verification_refs.locator: §3.2 Sound pressure level
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines sound pressure level as ten times the logarithm of squared sound pressure over squared reference pressure and states p0=20 μPa; its measurement method depends on measurement positions and acoustic environment.

facts.statement: A decibel level is a logarithmic ratio. Different sound levels therefore cannot generally be added arithmetically; combine the relevant mean-square pressure or sound-power quantities in linear form, then convert the total back to decibels.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 3747:2010, Acoustics — Determination of sound power levels and sound energy levels of noise sources using sound pressure
verification_refs.locator: §§3.2 and 3.17; sound pressure and sound power level definitions
verification_refs.supports_claim: Both levels are defined as logarithms of ratios of squared pressure or power; the logarithmic definitions imply summation must occur in the underlying linear energy/power domain.

facts.statement: For mutually uncorrelated sound sources expressed with a common reference and weighting, total level is Ltotal=10 log10(Σ10^(Li/10)) dB. This follows by converting each source level to a linear power or mean-square-pressure ratio, summing those quantities, and converting back; coherent correlated sources may require phase-aware pressure summation instead.

verification_refs.citation: Algebraic derivation of uncorrelated mean-square-pressure or acoustic-power addition
verification_refs.locator: Let Pi/P0=10^(Li/10); independent powers add, hence Ltotal=10 log10(Σ10^(Li/10))
verification_refs.supports_claim: The standard defines each level as 10 log10 of a linear power ratio (or squared-pressure ratio); substitution into linear power addition yields the stated expression under the stated uncorrelated-source condition.

facts.statement: Two equal-level, mutually uncorrelated sources with compatible weighting and reference combine to a level increase of 10 log10(2)=3.0103 dB over either source alone.

verification_refs.citation: Calculation from logarithmic level definition and independent-source power addition
verification_refs.supports_claim: Substitution into the standard's logarithmic power-level definition gives the stated 3.0103 dB increment; it assumes incoherent/uncorrelated power addition.

facts.statement: At the same reference pressure and with the same RMS and frequency/time weighting conventions, doubling sound-pressure amplitude changes sound pressure level by 20 log10(2)=6.0206 dB.

verification_refs.citation: Calculation from ISO 3747:2010 §3.2 sound pressure level definition
verification_refs.locator: ΔLp=20 log10(2prms/prms)=20 log10 2=6.0206 dB
verification_refs.supports_claim: The standard defines sound pressure level using 20 log10 of the RMS-pressure ratio; direct substitution of a factor of two gives 6.0206 dB.

facts.statement: Sound power level and sound pressure level are different quantities: sound power characterizes source emission, while sound pressure is measured at a point. Their numerical relationship requires an acoustic propagation/measurement model and conditions such as measurement surface or area, directivity, distance, environment, and applicable transmission or background corrections; they are not directly interchangeable without those conditions.

verification_refs.citation: ISO 3747:2010, Acoustics — Determination of sound power levels and sound energy levels of noise sources using sound pressure
verification_refs.locator: Scope and §§3.2, 3.17
verification_refs.supports_claim: The standard determines sound power by measuring sound pressure at defined positions in a specified reverberant environment and comparing with a calibrated reference source, demonstrating that sound power is not simply the point sound-pressure level.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Handbook 122, Noise Emission Measurements for Regulatory Purposes
verification_refs.locator: Equations (15)–(16), sound pressure-power relation in a reverberant room
verification_refs.supports_claim: The equation relating sound pressure level to sound power includes reverberation/time, volume, absorption and barometric-pressure terms, evidencing dependence on acoustic environment and geometry.

facts.statement: For Fisher 3582/3582i installations, the manual requires clean, dry and noncorrosive supply medium, specifies filtration guidance, and directs checking pressure connections for leaks; it identifies debris in the supply medium as a possible cause of positioner maintenance or repair. These are model-specific operating controls and do not establish that every listed contaminant causes failure in every positioner design.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher 3582 and 3582i Positioners and 582i Electro-Pneumatic Converter Instruction Manual, D200138X012
verification_refs.locator: Supply Connection and Specifications, PDF pp. 5–6 and 18–19; Maintenance introduction, PDF p. 36
verification_refs.supports_claim: Specifies clean, dry, noncorrosive supply medium and filtration; instructs checking pressure connections for leaks; states normal wear or external damage such as debris in supply medium may require maintenance or repair.

facts.statement: For the Fisher 657, bench-set pressure values adjust the actuator spring's initial compression and are checked on the actuator/valve assembly independently from positioner calibration, which sets the positioner's input-to-valve-travel relationship. Bench set and positioner calibration are distinct adjustments; exact procedures remain model-specific.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher 657 Diaphragm Actuator Instruction Manual, D100306X012
verification_refs.locator: Discussion of Bench Set and Spring Verification, PDF pp. 5–7
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual defines bench-set values as adjustment of initial actuator spring compression, checks the spring before the actuator stem is connected to the valve stem, and refers positioner installation/calibration to the separate positioner manual.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher 3582 and 3582i Positioners Instruction Manual, D200138X012
verification_refs.locator: Calibration section; zero and travel adjustment steps
verification_refs.supports_claim: The positioner manual's calibration procedure adjusts positioner zero and valve travel in response to input signal, distinct from the actuator spring bench set.

facts.statement: Emerson's control-valve terminology defines a bushing as supporting and/or guiding moving parts such as stems and plugs, and a cage as providing stability, guiding, balance, and alignment. In Ferrari's instrumented scale-one 2-inch globe-valve experiment, the transverse stem load was measured across selected flow rates, openings, and cavitation conditions; the study identifies such loads as relevant to wear prediction for valve and actuator guidance parts. The observed force is geometry- and condition-specific, and these sources do not establish a universal increase in actuator friction from eccentricity or stem bending.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 1: Introduction to Control Valves
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 1 terminology entries for Bushing and Cage
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines bushing support/guiding and cage stability, guiding, balance, and alignment functions.

verification_refs.citation: Jerome Ferrari, Measurement Of The Fluid Flow Load On A Globe Valve Stem Under Various Cavitation Conditions
verification_refs.locator: Abstract and experimental description, lines 3–5
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes why lateral-load evaluation matters for wear prediction of valve and actuator guidance parts and reports measured transverse forces for a scale-one 2-inch globe valve across selected test conditions.

facts.statement: For the cited Fisher balanced sliding-stem constructions, balancing reduces but does not make the actuator force calculation disappear: Catalog 14 distinguishes residual unbalance areas, specifies piston-ring friction forces to include in actuator sizing, and lists different available shutoff classes for Bore Seal versus piston-ring constructions. The Fisher EDR/ETR manual requires balance-hole inspection at every disassembly for service and removal of buildup or blockage. These are product-specific design and maintenance constraints, not universal limits for every balanced trim.

verification_refs.citation: Fisher Catalog 14, Actuator Sizing for Sliding-Stem Valves: Force Method
verification_refs.locator: Table 2H, p. B-8; Table 4A and additional-force instructions, pp. B-18–B-18.1
verification_refs.supports_claim: Table 2H presents distinct residual unbalance areas and shutoff-class labels for Fisher TBX/CVX Bore Seal and piston-ring constructions; the adjacent guidance requires piston-ring friction force to be included in actuator sizing and provides construction-dependent friction data.

verification_refs.citation: Fisher EDR and ETR Valves Instruction Manual D100391X012
verification_refs.locator: Trim Maintenance, p. 7, lines 324–327
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual says pressure balancing holes are necessary for proper and safe operation, directs inspection whenever the valve is disassembled for service, and requires removal of buildup, blockage, or clogging.

facts.statement: Fisher's sliding-stem actuator-sizing guidance determines packing friction from stem size, packing type, and the compressive load placed on packing by process pressure or bolting, and cautions that friction characteristics are not perfectly repeatable. Fisher's separate packing-selection guidance considers service pressure and temperature, leakage requirements, and required service life; these selection variables should not be misrepresented as a universal friction equation.

verification_refs.citation: Fisher Control Valve Sourcebook - Oil and Gas, packing selection and actuator sizing
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook directly lists stem size, packing type, and process/bolting compression as packing-friction determinants, states the friction is not fully repeatable, and separately frames packing selection by pressure, temperature, leakage requirement, service life, and friction characteristics.

facts.statement: In the control-valve model described by Valmet for a pneumatic-cylinder actuator, the friction coefficient can decrease substantially just after the valve starts moving; under the model's comparable contact conditions, this supports a breakaway-friction level greater than the initial running-friction level. This is not asserted as a universal ratio or as a long-dwell-time law.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet Flow Control Manual, §6 Mathematical simulation of control valve behavior, §6.5 Friction model
verification_refs.supports_claim: Valmet states that a large decrease in friction coefficient immediately after valve motion starts is an important factor for a pneumatic-cylinder-actuated control valve, and describes the velocity-dependent contact-friction model. This directly supports only that bounded model behavior.

facts.statement: For flowing control valves, force analysis includes dynamic fluid loads in addition to shutoff unbalance; in a full-scale instrumented 2-inch globe-valve model tested at selected flow rates, openings, and cavitation conditions, the transverse stem load reached the order of the axial load. A control-volume momentum balance attributes resultant force to pressure traction and momentum-flux change, while the measured magnitude remains specific to the tested valve and operating conditions.

verification_refs.citation: Fisher Control Valve Sourcebook - Oil and Gas, Actuator Sizing
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 2, pp. 2-7–2-8; extracted PDF lines 1593–1603
verification_refs.supports_claim: Manufacturer sizing guidance explicitly includes dynamic fluid forces and force gradients in addition to static fluid forces, friction, and seat loading, and says the force calculation varies by valve style and manufacturer.

verification_refs.citation: Jerome Ferrari, Measurement Of The Fluid Flow Load On A Globe Valve Stem Under Various Cavitation Conditions
verification_refs.locator: Abstract and experimental description, lines 3–5
verification_refs.supports_claim: An instrumented scale-one 2-inch globe-valve model was tested across selected cavitation conditions, flow rates, and disc positions; its transverse force could reach the order of its axial force. This supports occurrence and a bounded experimental comparison, not a universal magnitude.

verification_refs.citation: Integral linear-momentum balance for a fixed control volume
verification_refs.locator: The net external force equals the rate of momentum accumulation plus net momentum flux; pressure traction is included among external surface forces.
verification_refs.supports_claim: The pressure-force and momentum-flux terms are the control-volume basis for computing the resultant load; it does not assert a product-independent force magnitude.

facts.statement: For timestamped process data, preserve the event/source time separately from ingestion, server/processing, and persistence/append times when those semantics are available and relevant. The event/source timestamp should be assigned as close as practical to the value or event source and remain unchanged through forwarding; do not silently substitute arrival or storage time as if it were event time. Timestamp origin, clock basis, and fallback/absence must be documented because a source timestamp is not guaranteed to be available or accurate.

verification_refs.citation: OPC Foundation, OPC UA Part 4: Services, §7.11.3 SourceTimestamp
verification_refs.locator: §7.11.3 SourceTimestamp
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines SourceTimestamp as the timestamp applied by the value's data source, says it should indicate the last value/status change and should be generated as close as possible to the source; once assigned, forwarding servers do not change it. If the source is unavailable, SourceTimestamp is null.

verification_refs.citation: Apache Flink, Timely Stream Processing: Event Time and Processing Time
verification_refs.locator: Notions of Time: Event Time and Processing Time; Event Time and Watermarks
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines event time as when the event occurred on its producing device, typically embedded before entering the stream, and processing time as the system clock of the processing machine; explains that arrival order and outages can make processing-time results nondeterministic.

verification_refs.citation: Apache Kafka, ProducerRecord API
verification_refs.locator: Associated timestamp; CreateTime and LogAppendTime behavior
verification_refs.supports_claim: Separates producer record timestamp from broker log-append time: CreateTime preserves the producer timestamp, while LogAppendTime overwrites it with broker local time when appended. This is a concrete example of event/create and persistence/ingestion timestamps having different semantics.

facts.statement: ISA-95/IEC 62264 is a family of enterprise-control integration standards whose parts define models, terminology, activity models, interface information and—in a separate part—messaging services. It is not itself one universal wire-level communication protocol; implementations still select concrete transport and messaging technologies consistent with the applicable models/profiles.

verification_refs.citation: International Society of Automation, ISA-95 Standard: Enterprise-Control System Integration
verification_refs.locator: Part 1 Models and Terminology; Part 2 Objects and Attributes; Part 3 Activity Models; Part 6 Messaging Service Model
verification_refs.supports_claim: ISA describes Part 1 as models/terminology and functions/information at the interface, Part 2 as conceptual interface content, Part 3 as activity models and Part 6 as a messaging service model. The series' scope and multipart structure support the distinction from any one universal transport protocol.

verification_refs.citation: ISA InTech, The ISA-95 Enterprise-Control System Integration Standards
verification_refs.locator: Description of Parts 1 and 2, logical levels and integration boundaries
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that ISA-95 Parts 1 and 2 define primary data exchanges and a framework of models, with levels serving as logical integration boundaries; this corroborates the model/interface nature of the standard family.

facts.statement: A reference standard used to calibrate measurement equipment must be fit for the measurement's required accuracy/uncertainty and tolerance, with its identity, current calibration status, environmental conditions, handling/storage and use history controlled as required by the measurement program. Metrological traceability requires a documented calibration chain to stated references, with uncertainty contributions recorded at each link; no universal accuracy-ratio is implied.

verification_refs.citation: NIST, Metrological Traceability: Frequently Asked Questions and NIST Policy
verification_refs.locator: §3.1 Purpose; §5.2.1 Establishing Metrological Traceability
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines traceability as an unbroken documented calibration chain, each link contributing uncertainty; lists defined measurand, measurement system/working standard description, stated result and uncertainty, references used, and measurement assurance for status as elements of the chain.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Handbook 143, State Weights and Measures Laboratories Program Handbook, 5th edition
verification_refs.locator: §5.6.3.1 Reference standards; §5.6.3.3 Intermediate checks
verification_refs.supports_claim: Requires reference standards in its laboratory program to be calibrated by a traceability-capable body, calibrated before and after adjustment, and subject to scheduled intermediate checks that maintain confidence in calibration status. This is a concrete metrology-program control example.

verification_refs.citation: U.S. Department of Energy, Waste Isolation Pilot Plant, WP 10-AD3029, Calibration and Control of Monitoring and Data Collection Equipment
verification_refs.locator: §1.0 Master Database; §3.0 Calibration; §10.0 Storage
verification_refs.supports_claim: For plant/field M&DC equipment, establishes traceability to NIST/international/intrinsic standards, maintains item identification and calibration records, reviews certificates/data, and controls storage against specified environmental extremes. These are documented program controls, not universal site-specific procedures.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Handbook 150-16, NVLAP Calibration Laboratories Accreditation Requirements: Thermodynamic Metrology
verification_refs.locator: §5.6, equipment and reference standard records
verification_refs.supports_claim: Requires, in its laboratory-accreditation scope, documentation of reference standards and calibration environmental conditions, plus calibration certificate indications of uncertainty or accuracy tolerance limits and reference-standard traceability.

facts.statement: Calibration intervals are not universal fixed values: they should be selected and reviewed against the required measurement accuracy or criticality, applicable contract/regulatory limits, instrument stability and environment, use, manufacturer guidance, and as-found/history evidence. Interval changes require evidence that continued fitness is maintained; the applicable program governs the decision.

verification_refs.citation: NIST, Recommended Calibration Interval
verification_refs.locator: Factors determining intervals and measurement assurance program guidance
verification_refs.supports_claim: NIST states it does not set one general recalibration interval; interval depends on customer accuracy requirements, contract/regulation, inherent stability, and environmental factors. It recommends using measurement-assurance comparisons and analyzed data to characterize behavior and set/refine intervals.

verification_refs.citation: U.S. Department of Energy, Waste Isolation Pilot Plant, WP 10-AD3029, Calibration and Control of Monitoring and Data Collection Equipment
verification_refs.locator: §2.1.3 and §5.0–5.2, calibration recall frequency and as-found history
verification_refs.supports_claim: For this DOE facility's M&DC equipment, the procedure bases recall frequency on manufacturer recommendations, proposed use, and facility experience; records as-found calibration history and considers it when adjusting interval; it also requires analysis of as-found results. This is a documented implementation example, not a universal site-specific interval rule.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Handbook 145, Handbook for the Quality Assurance of Metrological Measurements
verification_refs.locator: §5.4, Intervals of Calibration
verification_refs.supports_claim: In its stated contractor quality-assurance context, calibration intervals are based on stability, purpose, and degree of use; prior results are used to shorten intervals or lengthen them only when accuracy will not be adversely affected.

facts.statement: In a calibration and quality program, preserve the instrument's as-found condition separately from its as-left condition after adjustment. If as-found results are out of tolerance, identify equipment or data potentially affected since the last calibration and assess impact under the applicable quality procedure; the assessment scope and corrective actions depend on the instrument use and governing requirements.

verification_refs.citation: U.S. Department of Energy, Waste Isolation Pilot Plant, WP 10-AD3029, Calibration and Control of Monitoring and Data Collection Equipment
verification_refs.locator: §5.0 Equipment Records; §8.0 Out-of-Tolerance Reporting, steps 8.2.1–8.2.2
verification_refs.supports_claim: The procedure requires calibration history to retain vendor as-found results; for OOT results it requires a usage list of potentially affected equipment/systems since the last calibration and evaluation of impact on equipment or collected data with corrective action as necessary. This is a documented quality-program example, not a claim that every jurisdiction adopts identical requirements.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Office of Weights and Measures, Field Standards for Weights and Measures, Article H-015
verification_refs.locator: Compliance Assessments, discussion of as-found and as-left calibration results
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that calibration certificates may report as-found and as-left results when an instrument is adjusted, and discusses the need to interpret the scope and basis of compliance statements rather than assume more than was assessed.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Handbook 145, Handbook for the Quality Assurance of Metrological Measurements
verification_refs.locator: §5.6, Out of Tolerance Evaluations
verification_refs.supports_claim: Requires a quality-assurance procedure to analyze the impact of out-of-tolerance measuring equipment on product quality, take corrective action, and retain the analysis and action records in the handbook's stated contractor context.

facts.statement: For a repairable asset under a defined observation and failure-counting basis, empirical MTBF is estimated as accumulated operating time divided by the number of qualifying failures. The failure definition and included operating-time boundary must be consistent; repair, waiting, and requalification time are not operating time in the NIST glossary definition.

verification_refs.citation: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §8.4.5.1, Constant repair rate (HPP/exponential) model
verification_refs.locator: Estimating the MTBF; total system operating time divided by total failures
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that the best MTBF estimate for the stated HPP/exponential model is total system operating time divided by total failures and gives the reciprocal failure-rate estimator.

verification_refs.citation: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Glossary: mean time between failures
verification_refs.locator: Entry: mean time between failures (MTBF)
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines MTBF as the average interval between failures and specifies that the average excludes time waiting for repair, under repair, and requalification, measuring only time available and operating.

verification_refs.citation: NASA Technical Reports Server, MTBF discussion and empirical definition
verification_refs.locator: Section: Mean Time Between Failures; empirical definition
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines empirical MTBF as total test hours divided by total observed failures and explains the constant-failure-rate model context; it also warns that MTBF is a mean, not a guaranteed failure-free operating interval.

facts.statement: For a simple repairable two-state model, inherent availability is A_i=MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR). This measure excludes preventive-maintenance and logistics/administrative delay; operational availability may include those additional downtime sources, so the formula must not be applied as a universal plant-availability equation.

verification_refs.citation: NASA Kennedy Space Center, Availability: What Is It?
verification_refs.locator: Steady-State Availability formulas; Inherent Availability, Achieved Availability, Operational Availability
verification_refs.supports_claim: Gives A_i=MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR), lists assumptions including constant failure and repair rates, says inherent availability excludes preventive maintenance, and distinguishes achieved/operational availability that include additional maintenance or logistics downtime.

verification_refs.citation: NASA Reliability and Maintainability Preferred Practice AT-3, Availability
verification_refs.locator: Inherent Availability equation and Achieved/Operational Availability definitions
verification_refs.supports_claim: Independently states the inherent availability equation and explicitly excludes administrative/logistic delay and preventive maintenance from MTTR for this measure; operational availability includes broader downtime.

facts.statement: Where a balanced trim communicates pressure through a finite-conductance passage into a chamber with finite fluid capacitance/compliance, chamber pressure has a transient response and need not equal its eventual steady value immediately during a rapid stroke or pressure transient. The time constant and force effect depend on the actual passage, fluid, chamber, and valve construction.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapters 3 and 5
verification_refs.locator: §3.1.1.3, Cage-Style Valve Bodies; §5.11.1.1, Unbalance Force
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes the balance pressure path and the plug force resulting from residual pressure differential; it supports the physical arrangement and relevance of chamber pressure, not a universal transient magnitude.

verification_refs.citation: Lumped pressure-node continuity model
verification_refs.locator: For finite conductance G and compliance C, C·dp/dt = G·(p_source−p); the first-order response has τ=C/G>0 and cannot jump instantaneously to the new steady pressure.
verification_refs.supports_claim: The stated bounded conclusion follows from the lumped pressure-node model under its explicit finite-conductance and finite-compliance assumptions. It does not establish a numerical time constant for a particular valve.

facts.statement: For a sliding control-valve assembly, breakaway/static friction is the force threshold to initiate relative motion, while running/dynamic friction opposes motion after it has begun. Their values depend on the contacting surfaces and normal load, so a universal fixed ratio should not be assumed.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 1: Introduction to Control Valves
verification_refs.locator: Terminology, Friction
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines static friction as the force that must be overcome before relative motion and dynamic/running friction as the force to maintain motion; states friction depends on normal force and the characteristics of the contacting surfaces. The handbook gives no universal conversion ratio, supporting the bounded instruction not to assume one.

facts.statement: In Fisher HP/HPA balanced-plug constructions covered by the cited manual, pressure-balancing holes are required for proper and safe operation and any buildup, blockage, or clogging is to be removed; blockage can therefore impair the intended pressure communication. The exact force and operating consequence is construction- and service-dependent.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher, HP and HPA Control Valves Instruction Manual
verification_refs.locator: Maintenance, Trim Replacement; note on pressure-balancing holes
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manual states that pressure-balancing holes in the valve plug are necessary for proper and safe operation, requires inspection at each disassembly, and directs removal of buildup, blockage, or clogging. This directly supports the construction-specific maintenance fact and the bounded inference that obstruction impairs the intended balancing pressure path; it does not establish a universal numeric force or dynamic response.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapters 3 and 5
verification_refs.locator: §3.1.1.3, Cage-Style Valve Bodies; §5.11.1.1, Unbalance Force
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes balanced constructions as communicating downstream pressure to both sides of the plug to reduce unbalanced force and relates residual force to net pressure differential and unbalance area; this provides the mechanism context without asserting the magnitude of blockage effects.

facts.statement: An unbalanced sliding-stem trim has no balancing pressure path that cancels most of the plug's static pressure force; the net pressure differential acts over the construction-specific unbalance area and loads the plug/stem assembly.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapters 3 and 5
verification_refs.locator: §3.1.1.3, Cage-Style Valve Bodies; §5.11.1.1, Unbalance Force
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook states balanced trim reduces most static unbalanced force by applying downstream pressure to both plug sides, and defines the remaining/unbalanced force as net pressure differential times net unbalance area; the unbalanced construction lacks that balancing cancellation path.

facts.statement: In the cited cage-style balanced globe-valve construction, the cage guides the plug, retains the seat ring, and characterizes flow; plug-to-cage seals limit the secondary leakage path, while balance passages communicate pressure across the plug to reduce static unbalance.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 3: Valve and Actuator Types
verification_refs.locator: §3.1.1.3, Cage-Style Valve Bodies
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook identifies cage-style trim functions as plug guiding, seat-ring retention and flow characterization; it describes plug-to-cage seals that limit upstream leakage and balanced designs where downstream pressure acts on both plug sides, reducing static unbalance.

facts.statement: The effective unbalance area is the equivalent net projected area over which the net pressure differential produces axial plug force; its value is construction-dependent and is not automatically the nominal seat area.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 5: Control Valve Sizing
verification_refs.locator: §5.11.1.1, Unbalance Force
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook defines unbalance force as net pressure differential times net unbalance area, notes area can include stem area depending on configuration, and gives different typical areas for unbalanced and balanced constructions.

verification_refs.citation: Resultant pressure force on a projected surface
verification_refs.locator: F_axial = integral(p n_axial dA); for uniform differential pressure, F = ΔP A_effective
verification_refs.supports_claim: The axial pressure resultant equals the pressure field integrated over the projected area; defining an equivalent area by F/ΔP yields the effective unbalance area.

facts.statement: If Fu=ΔP·Au and Fr=ΔP·Ar are evaluated at the same nonzero pressure differential and on the same static-force basis, then |Fr|/|Fu|=Ar/Au; this conditional area ratio is not an unconditional performance guarantee.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 5: Control Valve Sizing
verification_refs.locator: §5.11.1.1, Unbalance Force
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook gives unbalance force as net pressure differential times net unbalance area and notes balanced valves retain a small manufacturer-specific unbalance area.

verification_refs.citation: Ratio derivation from force-area relations
verification_refs.locator: |ΔP Ar|/|ΔP Au| = Ar/Au when common ΔP ≠ 0
verification_refs.supports_claim: Dividing the two force magnitudes cancels their shared nonzero pressure differential, leaving the area ratio.

facts.statement: Represent signed axial pressure force relative to an explicitly chosen positive stem axis; whether process pressure tends to open or close a sliding-stem valve is construction- and pressure/flow-orientation-dependent and must be determined from the actual configuration and manufacturer-specific diagrams or equations.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson Fisher, Actuator Sizing for Sliding-Stem Valves: Force Method
verification_refs.locator: Steps for determining pressure-tends-to-open or pressure-tends-to-close construction and corresponding force equations
verification_refs.supports_claim: The manufacturer instructs users to identify the actual construction using the supplied figures and then apply the matching equation; equations differ with flow/pressure orientation and plug/stem geometry.

verification_refs.citation: Signed force component in a selected coordinate system
verification_refs.locator: F_axial_signed = F_vector · e_positive_stem
verification_refs.supports_claim: A scalar sign for axial force is defined by projecting the force vector on the explicitly chosen positive stem-axis unit vector; the physical force direction itself follows the actual pressure geometry.

facts.statement: In cage-style balanced globe trims, the plug-to-cage seal forms a pressure boundary between pressure regions and limits leakage from the upstream/high-pressure region to the lower-pressure downstream region; this secondary seal is distinct from the plug-to-seat shutoff interface.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 3: Valve and Actuator Types
verification_refs.locator: §3.1.1.3, Cage-Style Valve Bodies
verification_refs.supports_claim: The handbook describes seals between the plug outer diameter and cage bore as limiting upstream high-pressure leakage to the lower-pressure downstream system.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Fabricated FB Valve Body Sizes and Trim Information
verification_refs.locator: Bore Seal Description
verification_refs.supports_claim: The bulletin identifies the plug-to-cage bore seal as blocking a secondary leakage path, distinct from contact of the plug with the seat ring to close the valve.

facts.statement: Leakage through the closed plug-seat interface and leakage through a plug-to-cage balance seal are separate physical paths; shutoff performance at the seat does not by itself establish the leakage condition of the secondary plug-to-cage path.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Fisher Fabricated FB Valve Body Sizes and Trim Information
verification_refs.locator: Bore Seal Description
