verification_refs.supports_claim: Confirms that process-piping code applicability includes cryogenic plants; component-specific material and toughness limits must be evaluated under the applicable code provisions rather than inferred from a generic temperature label.

verification_refs.citation: ASME, Impact Testing and Toughness Requirements for Pressure Vessels; ASME Section VIII, Divisions 1 & 2, course catalog
verification_refs.locator: Course description: toughness suitability at designated MDMT and conditional impact-test exemptions
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that pressure-vessel designers evaluate toughness and whether impact testing is required to demonstrate suitability at the designated MDMT, while qualifying conditions may exempt testing; this supports a code-specific review, not a universal test mandate.

verification_refs.citation: MSS SP-134, Valves for Cryogenic Service, Including Requirements for Body/Bonnet Extensions
verification_refs.edition_or_version: standard preview accessed 2026-10-12; verify governing edition in procurement documents
verification_refs.locator: Table of contents §§4–5 and §11; scope and low-temperature cryogenic testing
verification_refs.supports_claim: The standard's published contents and scope cover cryogenic-valve materials, design, and low-temperature testing; its test provisions are specification/agreement dependent, supporting review against the applicable valve standard and purchase specification.

facts.statement: Cryogenic extended bonnet은 packing과 actuator를 cold zone에서 분리하고 vapor space를 확보하기 위해 사용되며 required length와 orientation은 service별로 확인한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 6: Special and Severe Service Control Valves
verification_refs.locator: Cryogenic service discussion and Figure 6.5, Typical Extension Bonnet
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that frost can damage stem packing in cryogenic service and that an extension bonnet allows the packing box to be warmed by ambient temperatures; states that extension length depends on application temperature and insulation requirements. The evidence is manufacturer guidance and does not establish a universal length or orientation.

facts.statement: 고온·저온 서비스에서는 재질별 열팽창 차이로 stem과 trim의 상대 위치 또는 plug–cage 간극이 달라질 수 있다. 적용 온도와 조립 기준 온도를 확인하고 제조사 설계 간극·허용범위를 검토한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, CVX Steam Conditioning Valve product description
verification_refs.locator: Trim package: cage is allowed to grow during thermally induced excursions
verification_refs.supports_claim: A product-specific example of thermal growth affecting cage-guided trim design. It does not substantiate universal component-specific clearance values.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Sempell, Model 142 High Pressure Water Control Valve
verification_refs.locator: Product features: stem thermal expansion at high temperature differences
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies high-temperature stem thermal expansion as a design effect and describes a cup spring in the yoke head to accommodate it in this specific valve design.

facts.statement: Particle service는 size distribution, concentration, hardness, shape, density, settling tendency와 chemical behavior를 함께 정의한다.

verification_refs.citation: Metso, Basics in Minerals Processing, Slurry Valve Sizing
verification_refs.locator: Slurry valve sizing, particle characterization checklist
verification_refs.supports_claim: Lists particle size distribution, shape, hardness, and density/concentration among factors to consider for slurry valve and piping selection, and relates erosion to impact angle, velocity, cavitation, particle characteristics, and valve setting.

verification_refs.citation: Herianto et al., Erosion of sand screens by solid particles: a review of experimental investigations, Journal of Petroleum Exploration and Production Technology (2022), DOI 10.1007/s13202-022-01467-4
verification_refs.locator: Abstract and §§Essential factors affecting solid particle erosion / particle size distribution
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies particle shape, size, and concentration, plus flow and fluid properties, as interrelated erosion-test and service variables; discusses particle-size distribution, impact conditions, and limits of extrapolating simplified tests to field equipment.

verification_refs.citation: NIST Recommended Practice Guide: Particle Size Characterization
verification_refs.locator: Particle settling, density contrast, sample stability, and surface-chemistry discussion
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that settling velocity and particle-size characterization are affected by particle density relative to the fluid and by sample concentration, and that dissolution or other chemical/surface changes can alter sample properties; used here only to support including these properties when relevant to the actual process.

facts.statement: High local velocity는 specific kinetic-energy level과 impingement intensity를 높일 수 있으므로 flow direction과 local geometry를 함께 평가한다.

verification_refs.citation: Woodson and Melcher, Electromechanical Dynamics, Part II: Fields, Forces, and Motion, MIT OpenCourseWare textbook, §13.1.2
verification_refs.locator: §13.1.2, kinetic energy density of a moving fluid
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines fluid kinetic energy density as one half times density times velocity squared; the quadratic relation supports the direction of change with local velocity, not a direct erosion-rate prediction.

verification_refs.citation: Hutchings et al., The impact angle dependence of erosion damage caused by solid particle impact, Wear 203–204 (1997), 573–579, DOI 10.1016/S0043-1648(96)07430-3
verification_refs.locator: Abstract and experimental variables: particle impact velocity, impact angle, material hardness, and test geometry
verification_refs.supports_claim: Experimental results characterize erosion as dependent on impact angle, particle impact velocity, and material hardness; the tests explicitly used geometry to establish impact angles, showing why impingement intensity is local and geometry-dependent.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet, Control Valve Handbook / Flow Control Manual
verification_refs.locator: Flow velocity and flashing-flow erosion discussion
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that erosion is strongly dependent on flow velocity and describes flashing damage as high-velocity liquid droplets impinging on valve body and trim; it supports a conditional erosion exposure concern rather than a universal damage rate.

facts.statement: Valve outlet jet, reducer, elbow와 downstream-pipe diameter는 velocity recovery, vibration, erosion와 noise의 위치를 바꿀 수 있다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 5: Control Valve Sizing
verification_refs.locator: §5.8, attached fittings and inlet/outlet reducers
verification_refs.supports_claim: Includes upstream/downstream fitting and reducer resistance effects in installed valve sizing, establishing that attached piping geometry changes the local pressure/velocity conditions at the valve.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet, Flow Control Manual, Liquid Flow
verification_refs.locator: §§3.3.2–3.4, downstream flashing/cavitation, noise, and location control
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes bubble-collapse and associated noise/damage shifting downstream under flashing/cavitation conditions, and recommends considering downstream piping length and flow orientation; effects remain service-specific.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet, Flow Control Manual, Appendices: Manifold Design Guidelines for Valves
verification_refs.locator: Appendix M, manifold design guidelines
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that pumps, joints, and elbows can disturb flow patterns and affect control-valve performance, and that adequate straight pipe may be needed to obtain a suitable velocity profile.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet, Modern software for intelligent valve sizing
verification_refs.locator: Sections: Flow velocity & erosion; Noise
verification_refs.supports_claim: Reports erosion on valve trim, body, and downstream piping under erosive/flashing service and links high exit velocity with aerodynamic noise and potential vibration damage, supporting evaluation of the full assembly rather than the valve body alone.

facts.statement: Micro-flow passage는 particle, polymerization, contamination와 deposit에 의해 plugging되기 쉬우므로 filtration, cleanability와 spare strategy를 검토한다.

verification_refs.citation: SAMSON, Type 3510 Micro-flow Valve, Operating Instructions E8091
verification_refs.locator: Required conditions / Selection: filter warning for solids that could block the valve
verification_refs.supports_claim: For this micro-flow valve model, instructs that a filter be installed when solids could block the valve, while warning that the filter may block flow for the specified fail-safe configuration; this supports service-specific blockage review and explicitly rules out universal filtration advice.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet/Neles, Application Report 2722_08_01 EN, Polymer Slurry and Polymerization Valve Solutions
verification_refs.locator: Neles solution for polymer slurry; polymer build-up prevention at small openings
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes polymer build-up and seizure risk in specific polymerization applications and identifies trim designs intended to resist plugging at small openings; the application-specific nature is retained in the fact conditions.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet, Flow Control Manual, Multi-phase Flow §5.4 Slurries
verification_refs.locator: §5.4, slurry flow through conventional control valves
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies erosion and plugging as possible mechanical problems in conventional-valve handling of gas-solid slurry, without asserting that plugging occurs in every slurry service.

facts.statement: Cavitation, flashing와 aerodynamic·hydrodynamic noise는 severe-service risk를 구성할 수 있으나 physics, prediction와 mitigation 상세는 Topic 8과 Topic 9가 소유한다.

verification_refs.citation: Valmet, Flow Control Manual, Liquid Flow
verification_refs.locator: §§3.3–3.4, cavitation, flashing, erosion, vibration and hydrodynamic noise
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that cavitation and flashing can produce erosion, vibration and noise, with damage and collapse location dependent on flow regime, velocity, material and valve/downstream geometry; it does not imply every such service fails.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Fisher, Control Valve Handbook, Chapter 5: Control Valve Sizing
verification_refs.locator: §5.11, aerodynamic noise prediction and pressure-ratio regimes
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes aerodynamic noise generation as a function of valve geometry and service conditions and distinguishes source and path treatment; supports the separate risk category without a universal noise threshold claim.

facts.statement: 산업 무선망은 배치 전에 site survey로 거리, 구조물, 차폐, 반사, 이동설비, 간섭원, 공존채널과 설치높이를 조사하고 설치 후 실제 link 상태를 검증해야 한다.

verification_refs.citation: R. Candell et al., NIST Advanced Manufacturing Series 300-4, Guide to Industrial Wireless Systems Deployments
verification_refs.locator: §4.2 Factory Survey; §§4.4.1–4.4.4 Solution Design/Frequency Planning/QoS/Frequency Harmonization; §§4.5.1.1 and 4.5.1.5; §4.5.2 Network Monitoring; §§7.3–7.4
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines factory survey as an early deployment step and calls for assessment of physical environment, RF propagation, spectrum, interference, and factory inventory; explains distance/material/frequency effects, metal reflections, changing environments, channel utilization and frequency planning; recommends antenna positioning above machinery/obstructions, installed-device black-box tests, and monitoring of node status, routes, link health/errors, spectrum, and network performance.

verification_refs.citation: FieldComm Group, WirelessHART Deployment Methodology and Guidelines Webinar
verification_refs.locator: Site Walkdown and Network Deployment/Commissioning sections, slide 13 and webinar agenda
verification_refs.supports_claim: Recommends planned coexistence with other wireless protocols, separation of antennas, and a site walkdown locating WirelessHART applications, existing Wi-Fi/other wireless antennas, backhaul access, and gateway power. The webinar deployment method covers network deployment, commissioning, maintenance, and acceptance performance criteria; those recommendations are WirelessHART-specific examples.

facts.statement: Deadband는 Alarm이 발생한 뒤 정상 복귀 임계값을 발생 임계값과 다르게 두는 값의 이력폭으로, 경계 부근 노이즈에 의한 반복 발생과 해제를 줄인다.

verification_refs.citation: Rockwell Automation, Library of Process Objects: Display Elements, Publication PROCES-RM014F-EN-P
verification_refs.locator: Alarm maintenance-tab description, p. 104
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines alarm deadband as hysteresis applied to an alarm limit; gives a high alarm example where the alarm activates above 90 and clears below 85 with a deadband of 5; states this helps prevent a noisy signal from generating numerous spurious alarms.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Rosemount Analytical, OPM 2000R Transmissometer Instruction Manual
verification_refs.locator: §6.4.2, Table 6-16, AL1/AL2 Deadband
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines the deadband as the amount subtracted from a high alarm setpoint before deactivation and states that the feature is designed to prevent a chattering alarm; the example is product-specific.

verification_refs.citation: ISA-TR18.2.5-2022, Alarm System Monitoring, Assessment, and Auditing
verification_refs.locator: §3.1.2, definition of active alarm and Note 1
verification_refs.supports_claim: Notes that deadband, on/off delays and latching can make an alarm remain active after its condition becomes false or remain inactive while the condition is true, supporting the distinction between alarm condition and alarm state created by hysteresis.

facts.statement: Alarm priority는 단순 측정값 크기가 아니라 조치하지 않았을 때의 결과 심각도와 운전자에게 허용된 응답시간을 함께 평가하여 결정하며, 우선순위별 표시와 대응절차가 일관되어야 한다.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson, Alarm Rationalization, DeltaV Alarm Management White Paper
verification_refs.locator: Alarm prioritization method, printed p. 9
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that alarm priority is typically determined using a matrix with two inputs: severity of the potential direct consequence and time available for operator response before the consequence can no longer be prevented; highest priorities correspond to more severe consequences and shorter response time.

verification_refs.citation: ISA-TR18.2.2-2016, Alarm Identification and Rationalization
verification_refs.locator: §7.1, Consequence/allowable operator response time method (contents preview)
verification_refs.supports_claim: The official ISA report contents identify a dedicated prioritization method combining consequence with allowable operator response time, corroborating the method name and scope. The detailed matrix and site-specific categories are not claimed from the contents preview.

verification_refs.citation: D. G. Dunn and N. P. Sands, Alarm management questions that everyone asks, ISA InTech
verification_refs.locator: Rationalization discussion, lines 176–179
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that rationalization documents alarm consequence, response time, operator action, priority and related alarm attributes; it describes prioritization as supporting the operator and distinguishes it from alarm classification.

facts.statement: Alarm의 Process condition, Active·Return-to-normal 상태와 Acknowledgement 상태는 별개이며, 운전자 Acknowledge는 인지 기록일 뿐 원인 제거 또는 Alarm 조건 해제를 의미하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: Rockwell Automation, FactoryTalk Alarms and Events System Configuration Guide, Publication FTAE-RM001R-EN-E
verification_refs.locator: Chapter 10, Monitor and interact with alarms at runtime, Acknowledge an alarm, printed p. 98
verification_refs.supports_claim: States that acknowledging an alarm indicates operator awareness but does not correct the condition causing it.

verification_refs.citation: Rockwell Automation, SLC Software Installation and Configuration Guide, Publication SIG NE-UM001A-EN-P
verification_refs.locator: §2.6 Alarm/Fault Handling, printed p. 47
verification_refs.supports_claim: Documents that acknowledgement time is recorded while an active alarm remains in the active summary until the condition clears; alarm state and acknowledgement state are therefore separate in this implementation.

verification_refs.citation: Emerson/Rosemount, MON2020 User Manual MS-00809-0100-2020
verification_refs.locator: §6.1.2 Acknowledge and clear alarms, printed pp. 150–152
verification_refs.supports_claim: Displays alarm acknowledgement status separately from ACTIVE/INACTIVE state and states an alarm remains active until the value leaves the alarm state; this source is a product-specific example.

facts.statement: Precision은 모델이 Positive로 판정한 사례 중 실제 Positive의 비율이며 오경보가 많은 경우 낮아진다.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn, precision_score API reference
verification_refs.locator: Definition and Notes
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines precision as tp/(tp+fp), describes it as the ability not to label negative samples positive, and documents the zero-positive-prediction undefined-metric case.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn User Guide, Metrics and scoring: quantifying the quality of predictions
verification_refs.locator: §3.4.4.9.1 Binary classification
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines TP and FP in the binary confusion matrix and precision as TP/(TP+FP), supporting the stated false-positive relationship.

facts.statement: Recall은 실제 Positive 중 모델이 검출한 비율이며 위험 고장의 미검출이 중요한 경우 핵심 지표가 된다.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn, recall_score API reference
verification_refs.locator: Definition and Notes
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines recall as TP/(TP+FN) and describes it as the classifier's ability to find positive samples; documents undefined/zero-division handling.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn User Guide, Metrics and scoring: quantifying the quality of predictions
verification_refs.locator: §3.4.4.9.1 Binary classification
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines false negatives as missing results and recall as TP/(TP+FN); the high-consequence relevance is conditional application of this metric, not a universal requirement.

facts.statement: Binary Classification은 TP, FP, TN, FN의 Confusion Matrix로 결과를 구분하여 오경보와 미검출을 별도로 해석해야 한다.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn User Guide, Metrics and scoring: quantifying the quality of predictions
verification_refs.locator: §3.4.4.9.1 Binary classification
verification_refs.supports_claim: Presents the binary-classification table of TP, FP, TN, and FN, labels FP as unexpected and FN as missing result, and defines precision/recall from these counts.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn, confusion_matrix API reference
verification_refs.locator: Definition and binary-classification examples
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines confusion-matrix entries by actual and predicted class and documents the TN/FP/FN/TP binary layout.

facts.statement: F1 Score는 Precision과 Recall의 조화평균으로 두 지표의 균형을 요약하지만 비용과 운전조건을 단독으로 대체하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn, f1_score API reference
verification_refs.locator: Definition and F1 formula
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines F1 as the harmonic mean of precision and recall and gives its TP/FP/FN formula; the formula contains no application-specific cost or process-operating-condition input.

verification_refs.citation: scikit-learn User Guide, Metrics and scoring: quantifying the quality of predictions
verification_refs.locator: §3.4 scoring API; §§3.4.4.9.1–3.4.4.9.2 classification metrics
verification_refs.supports_claim: Documents that evaluation tools use a selected scoring metric and that F-measures summarize precision/recall; this supports treating F1 as one metric rather than a substitute for application-specific acceptance criteria.

facts.statement: 온도 적격성 시험은 사용(비포장)과 운송·보관(포장) 조건, 통전 여부 및 발열 시편 여부를 구분해 냉·건열 시험을 선정한다. 온도 변화 자체의 영향은 IEC 60068-2-1/-2의 안정상태 시험과 별도 방법으로 평가한다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-1:2013, Environmental testing — Part 1: General and guidance
verification_refs.locator: Scope and environmental test tailoring framework
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes methods and severities for assessing expected transportation, storage and operational use, and provides a tailoring framework for choosing tests and severities.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-2-2:2025, Environmental testing — Part 2-2: Tests — Test B: Dry heat
verification_refs.locator: Scope
verification_refs.supports_claim: Covers heat-dissipating and non-heat-dissipating specimens, energized and non-energized specimens normally reaching temperature stability, and packed/unpacked conditions simulating transport/storage or use. It distinguishes dry-heat capability from temperature-change testing.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-2-1:2025, Environmental testing — Part 2-1: Tests — Test A: Cold
verification_refs.locator: Scope
verification_refs.supports_claim: Covers heat-dissipating and non-heat-dissipating specimens, energized/non-energized testing when temperature stability is normally achieved, and packed/unpacked conditions for transport/storage or use; it does not itself assess temperature-change effects.

facts.statement: Qualification 시험조건은 적용 제품규격, 프로젝트 specification, 설치환경과 equipment intended use에서 추적되어야 하며 근거 없이 severity나 duration을 임의 선정하지 않는다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-1:2013, Environmental testing — Part 1: General and guidance
verification_refs.locator: Scope and Annex C environmental test tailoring framework
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes methods and severities for expected transportation, storage and operational use, and a tailoring framework to select appropriate tests and severities for test specifications. It does not prescribe one universal profile for all equipment.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-2-2:2025, Environmental testing — Part 2-2: Tests — Test B: Dry heat
verification_refs.locator: Scope and edition changes
verification_refs.supports_claim: Differentiates use versus transport/storage conditions and states that 2025 test-report requirements are standardized for the selected dry-heat test method; this illustrates method-specific test planning rather than a universal qualification profile.

facts.statement: Vibration 시험의 fixture, mounting torque, orientation, cable restraint와 sensor location은 실제 설치조건을 대표해야 하며 fixture resonance나 과도한 cable support가 DUT 결과를 왜곡하지 않도록 한다.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-2-47:2005, Environmental testing — Part 2-47: Test — Mounting of specimens for vibration, impact and similar dynamic tests
verification_refs.locator: Clauses 5–6 (mounting components and equipment); clause 6 and mounting torque provisions
verification_refs.supports_claim: Requires equipment to be mechanically connected directly or via a rigid fixture; the relevant specification states when the normal mounting structure is used, avoids additional stays, requires cables/pipes to impose restraint and mass similar to normal use, and specifies fixing-bolt size and mounting torque. A rigid fixture has no resonance within the test range or meets tolerances at all fixing points.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-2-47:2005 standard text preview, supplied by Slovenian Institute for Standardization (SIST)
verification_refs.locator: Clauses 5–6
verification_refs.supports_claim: Provides the operative mounting text on representative normal mounting, restraint and mass of attached cables/pipes, rigid fixture resonance, and specified bolt size/mounting torque.

verification_refs.citation: IEC 60068-2-6:2007, Environmental testing — Part 2-6: Tests — Test Fc: Vibration (sinusoidal)
verification_refs.locator: Clause 3 definitions and test setup; refers to IEC 60068-2-47 for mounting
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines fixing points as locations where the specimen is normally fastened in service and defines vibration check/measurement points used to control or gather test data; references IEC 60068-2-47 for mounting.

facts.statement: Signed travel error는 ex=xcmd-xmeas로 정의하고 sign convention을 일관되게 유지한다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible signed-error definition check
verification_refs.locator: ex=xcmd-xmeas; xcmd=50, xmeas=47 gives ex=+3 in the common travel unit
verification_refs.supports_claim: The stated expression implements the explicitly chosen command-minus-measurement sign convention; substitution yields +3 for command 50 and measured travel 47. The sign is a declared convention, not a universal industry convention.

facts.statement: Full-span travel error는 EFS=100(xcmd-xmeas)/(xmax-xmin)이며 xmax>xmin domain을 갖는다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible normalized-error definition check
verification_refs.locator: EFS=100(xcmd-xmeas)/(xmax-xmin); xcmd=50, xmeas=47, xmin=0, xmax=100 gives 3%
verification_refs.supports_claim: The positive span condition prevents a zero or negative normalization denominator. Numerator and denominator share travel units, so the ratio is dimensionless and multiplication by 100 expresses percent. The example evaluates to 3%.

facts.statement: 동일 command와 comparable condition에서 H(u)=|xup(u)-xdown(u)|로 upstroke·downstroke hysteresis를 계산한다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible travel-loop hysteresis definition check
verification_refs.locator: H(u)=|xup(u)-xdown(u)|; xup=52%, xdown=48% gives 4 percentage points
verification_refs.supports_claim: At the same command and comparable conditions, the absolute difference gives a nonnegative magnitude of branch separation; the example is 4 percentage points. It does not identify the physical cause of the hysteresis.

facts.statement: Context-conditioned baseline residual은 rz=zcurrent-zbaseline(context)로 정의한다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible residual definition check
verification_refs.locator: rz=zcurrent-zbaseline(context); 1.3-1.0=+0.3
verification_refs.supports_claim: The equation is the explicitly defined signed current-minus-baseline residual. Matching the context and units makes the subtraction interpretable; the example yields +0.3. The sign convention is definition-specific.

facts.statement: Rate of change는 (z2-z1)/(t2-t1)이며 t2>t1 domain과 consistent sampling window를 사용한다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible finite-difference rate check
verification_refs.locator: (z2-z1)/(t2-t1); z1=2, z2=5, t1=1, t2=4 gives 1 feature-unit/time-unit
verification_refs.supports_claim: The expression is a two-point finite-difference rate. Requiring t2>t1 prevents division by zero and fixes chronological order; the example evaluates to 1 feature-unit per time-unit. It is not a smoothed derivative estimator.

facts.statement: Accumulated travel은 TAT=Σ|xk-xk-1|로 계산할 수 있으며 sampling·normalization basis를 기록한다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible sampled-total-variation check
verification_refs.locator: Σ|xk-xk-1|; samples [0, 10, 4, 8] yield |10-0|+|4-10|+|8-4|=20 travel units
verification_refs.supports_claim: Summing absolute successive differences counts both forward and reverse travel without cancellation. The example sequence yields 20 units. The sampled value depends on sampling; it does not capture motion that is not represented between samples, so basis and normalization must be reported.

facts.statement: 동일 position에서 opening·closing actuator pressure band를 ΔPsig(x)=|Popen(x)-Pclose(x)|로 비교할 수 있다.

verification_refs.citation: Reproducible same-position pressure-band definition check
verification_refs.locator: ΔPsig(x)=|Popen(x)-Pclose(x)|; 120 kPa and 108 kPa yield a 12 kPa magnitude
verification_refs.supports_claim: At a matched position and comparable conditions, the absolute difference is a nonnegative pressure-band magnitude with the same pressure unit. This metric alone does not identify friction or another physical cause.

facts.statement: 수리가능 시스템의 단순 정상상태 고유가용도는 일정 고장률·수리율과 평균시간 가정에서 A = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR)로 평가할 수 있다.

verification_refs.citation: Two-state repairable-system steady-state derivation
verification_refs.locator: For failure rate λ and repair rate μ, A=μ/(λ+μ); with MTBF=1/λ and MTTR=1/μ, substitution gives MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR)
verification_refs.supports_claim: The two-state up/down model yields steady-state up probability μ/(λ+μ). Substituting the constant-rate mean times gives MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR). This is a simple inherent-availability model and excludes planned downtime, logistics delays, and redundant-system effects.

facts.statement: 독립고장 가정에서 직렬구조 신뢰도는 구성요소 신뢰도의 곱으로 감소하고, 병렬 이중화는 동시고장 확률을 줄이지만 공통원인고장을 별도로 반영해야 한다.

verification_refs.supports_claim: The series product follows from independence and requiring all components to succeed. Parallel success is the complement of simultaneous independent channel failures. A common cause violates the independent-failure model and must be included separately rather than assumed away.

facts.statement: Reliability는 정해진 조건과 기간 동안 요구기능을 고장 없이 수행할 확률이며 시간구간을 포함하는 개념이다.

facts.statement: Maintainability는 정해진 조건에서 고장난 시스템을 규정시간 내 복구할 수 있는 능력이며 진단성, 접근성, 모듈교체와 절차 표준화에 좌우된다.

facts.statement: Availability는 요구 시점에 시스템이 기능을 수행할 수 있는 확률 또는 시간비율이며 고장빈도와 복구시간의 영향을 함께 받는다.

verification_refs.locator: Clause 4.5.4, PDF p. 14

It states maintainability influences availability through maintenance speed/downtime and preventive maintenance can prevent unexpected failures, supporting the stated failure/restoration influence while leaving the exact measure profile-specific.

facts.statement: Common Cause Failure는 공유 원인 하나가 다중 채널을 함께 고장내는 현상으로 동일 설계결함, 공통전원, 환경, 소프트웨어, 유지보수 오류가 원인이 될 수 있다.

verification_refs.locator: CCF event criteria
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines a CCF event as two or more components failed or degraded within a selected period because of a single shared cause and coupling mechanism, directly supporting the core definition.

verification_refs.citation: U.S. NRC Regulatory Issue Summary 99-03, Resolution of Generic Issue 145, Actions to Reduce Common-Cause Failures
verification_refs.locator: CCF event insights and coupling-factor examples
verification_refs.supports_claim: Identifies shared hardware design defects, incorrect calibration-procedure setpoints, and environmental fuel-oil contamination as coupling examples; it also describes maintenance/test discoveries and human errors affecting redundant trains. These support the anchor's non-exhaustive design, environment, and maintenance examples.

verification_refs.locator: Section 19.1.3.1.5.1.3, Digital I&C System Software Reliability
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that the same programs executed in parallel channels can cause a software fault to produce common-mode failure in all channels, supporting software as a possible shared cause under the stated condition.

verification_refs.locator: Recommendations on DC power division independence, bus ties, testing and maintenance
verification_refs.supports_claim: Discusses redundant safety-related DC power divisions and design/operational features that can compromise their independence, supporting shared power as a possible common-cause coupling factor rather than claiming every common supply causes failure.

facts.statement: 통신시스템은 물리매체, 신호·링크, 전송·응용 프로토콜, 장치 프로파일과 정보모델의 계층으로 나누어 보아야 하며, 같은 케이블이나 Ethernet을 사용해도 상위 계층이 다르면 직접 상호운용되지 않을 수 있다.

verification_refs.supports_claim: Specifies how the Modbus application protocol is carried over TCP/IP on Ethernet-connected devices, corroborating that Ethernet connectivity alone does not provide application protocol compatibility.

facts.statement: Device profile은 장치 class별 필수·선택 기능, parameter, status와 동작규칙을 공통화하여 host와 다중 vendor 장치의 기능 상호운용성을 높인다.

This supports the interoperability benefit while bounding it to the selected profile and functionality.

facts.statement: 예측확률은 Calibration을 확인해야 하며 Confidence 또는 Probability가 실제 발생빈도와 일치하지 않으면 Threshold와 Risk 판단이 왜곡될 수 있다.

verification_refs.locator: §1.16 and §1.16.1, calibration curves
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines a well-calibrated binary classifier as one whose predictions near probability p occur positive approximately p fraction of the time, and explains that calibration curves compare predicted probabilities with observed positive frequencies. It also warns that classifiers may provide poor probability estimates.

verification_refs.citation: Expected-loss derivation for binary decisions with calibrated event probability
verification_refs.locator: With false-positive cost C_FP and false-negative cost C_FN, L(positive)=(1-p)C_FP and L(negative)=pC_FN; select positive when p≥C_FP/(C_FP+C_FN).
verification_refs.supports_claim: If the probability supplied to a cost-derived threshold differs from the actual conditional event frequency, the expected-loss comparison can select the wrong action. Example: C_FP=7 and C_FN=3 gives threshold 0.7; a forecast 0.8 with actual event frequency 0.5 selects positive although expected positive-action loss is 3.5 and negative-action loss is 1.5. This demonstrates that miscalibration can distort threshold/risk decisions, without asserting calibration alone selects the threshold.

facts.statement: Training Set은 Parameter 학습에, Validation Set은 Model과 Hyperparameter 선택에, Test Set은 최종 일반화 성능 확인에 사용하며 역할을 분리한다.

facts.statement: 산업 시계열은 시간순 분할과 설비·Batch·제품 단위 Group 분할을 적용하여 동일 Episode와 미래정보가 Train과 Test에 섞이지 않게 해야 한다.

This supports grouping by the actual dependent unit, not an arbitrary label.

facts.statement: Supervised learning은 입력 데이터와 대응하는 target/label을 이용해 예측 관계를 학습한다. Classification은 이산 범주의 target을, regression은 연속값 target을 예측하며, forecasting도 target과 시간 구조를 정한 예측 문제로 구성할 수 있다.

facts.statement: Unsupervised learning은 학습 입력에 대응하는 target/label을 지정하지 않고 데이터의 구조나 표현을 학습한다. 군집화 등으로 구조를 탐색할 수 있지만, 발견된 구조가 현장 고장원인이나 정비 의미를 자동으로 입증하지 않으므로 별도 검증이 필요하다.

verification_refs.locator: Overview
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes clustering as an unsupervised task that groups samples based on similarity, without supplying class labels.

facts.statement: Classification은 이산 범주의 target을, regression은 연속 수치 target을 예측한다. Forecasting은 시간 순서가 있는 자료의 미래 target을 예측하는 문제로 정의할 수 있으며, 모델·평가 분할은 예측시점과 실제 의사결정 목적에 맞춰야 한다.

verification_refs.locator: §3.1.2.6, time-series cross-validation
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that time-series evaluation should respect temporal ordering and evaluate on future observations when estimating deployment generalization.

facts.statement: 일부 anomaly/novelty detector는 관측치의 abnormality score를 계산하고 decision threshold로 inlier/outlier 판정을 만든다. 해당 판정은 통계적 이상 여부이지 특정 고장원인의 확정 진단은 아니며, threshold는 estimator와 오경보·미검출 비용 및 현장 검증 조건에 맞춰야 한다.

verification_refs.locator: Overview and API behavior
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes outlier and novelty detection as identifying unusual observations; shows scoring functions and threshold-based inlier/outlier prediction, with threshold behavior controlled by estimator-specific parameters. It does not identify a physical failure cause.

facts.statement: Predictive maintenance는 온도·소음·진동 등 관측된 설비 상태자료를 이용한 고장 예측을 바탕으로 정비를 시작하거나 계획하는 접근이다. 예측과 정비 판단을 지원하는 것이며, 고장 제거 또는 고장 방지를 보장하지 않는다.

verification_refs.locator: §2.1, Literature on Predictive Maintenance Economics
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines predictive maintenance as analogous to condition-based maintenance and initiated based on failure predictions using observed data such as temperature, noise, and vibration.

verification_refs.citation: NIST, Manufacturing Machinery Maintenance
verification_refs.locator: Maintenance types, predictive maintenance
verification_refs.supports_claim: Describes predictive maintenance as condition-based maintenance initiated on failure predictions from observed data, distinguishing it from time/cycle-scheduled preventive maintenance and post-failure reactive maintenance.

facts.statement: Remaining Useful Life(RUL)는 기준 시점의 상태·사용 이력으로부터 기능적 고장 또는 정의된 end-of-life 기준에 도달할 때까지의 잔여 사용시간/사이클을 추정한 값이다. 추정은 상태·모델·센서·미래 운전조건의 불확실성을 포함하며, 결과는 해당 failure threshold와 적용조건에 종속되므로 불확실성 범위와 조건을 함께 해석해야 한다.

verification_refs.locator: §§I–III, RUL definition, end-of-life threshold and uncertainty propagation
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines RUL at a prediction instant as condition-based usage time remaining until failure based on measurements and past use; estimates future health and crossing of a functional failure threshold, considering future usage conditions and uncertainty.

verification_refs.citation: NASA, Prognostics: Damage Threshold and Uncertainty Characterization
verification_refs.supports_claim: Explains that an end-of-life threshold is a measurable condition that need not mean total destruction and that RUL estimates without quantified uncertainty bounds have limited decision value.

facts.statement: 시계열 feature engineering은 예측시점에 사용 가능한 과거 관측으로 lag, rolling 통계량 등 입력 특징을 만들 수 있다. 미래 관측을 포함한 특징이나 시간순서를 무시한 평가 split은 누설을 일으켜 실제 미래 예측 성능을 과대평가할 수 있다.

verification_refs.supports_claim: Demonstrates lagged values and shifted rolling statistics as predictors of a future target and warns that random splitting can cheat by using temporally later training observations; proper evaluation respects time structure.

verification_refs.locator: §12.2, Data leakage
verification_refs.supports_claim: Defines leakage in terms of using information unavailable at prediction time and explains that test-informed preprocessing or feature selection can create optimistic evaluation.

facts.statement: 학습·평가 자료는 의도된 설비·운전·배포 맥락에 적합하고 그 맥락을 대표하는지 점검해야 한다. 정상/고장 상태, 운전모드, 제품, 계절, 정비상태, 센서 품질 등은 적용 분야에서 대표성에 영향을 주는 후보 차원이지 모든 프로젝트의 고정 필수목록은 아니다. 자료 선택·수집 맥락, 데이터 품질, ground-truth/label의 한계와 편향을 기록한다.

facts.statement: 고장·이상처럼 희소한 positive class에서는 Accuracy만 보면 다수 정상 class를 맞히는 성능에 가려 검출 성능이 과대평가될 수 있다. PR curve/precision-recall, per-class recall 또는 balanced accuracy 등 목적에 맞는 지표를 함께 살피고, class weighting이나 sampling은 학습 시도 후보로 두되 실제 운전 threshold·비용과 대표적인 평가자료에서 효과를 확인해야 한다.

facts.statement: 이진 분류에서 양성 class의 score threshold를 낮추면 양성 판정이 약해지지 않고 추가 사례가 포함되어 recall이 낮아지지 않으며, 추가된 사례 중 실제 음성이 있으면 false positive가 증가하고 precision이 낮아질 수 있다. threshold는 false negative 비용, false positive 비용, 후속 확인인력·정비부하 등 현장 목적에 맞는 metric/utility로 검증해야 하며 단일 보편 최적값은 없다.
